The **violoncello** ( [*VY-ə-lən-CHEL-oh*](/wiki/Help:Pronunciation_respelling_key "Help:Pronunciation respelling key"), Italian pronunciation: [[vjolonˈtʃɛllo]](/wiki/Help:IPA/Italian "Help:IPA/Italian")),[[1]](#cite_note-1) commonly abbreviated as **cello** ( [*CHEL-oh*](/wiki/Help:Pronunciation_respelling_key "Help:Pronunciation respelling key")), is a middle pitched bowed (sometimes [plucked](/wiki/Pizzicato "Pizzicato") and occasionally [hit](/wiki/Col_legno "Col legno")) [string instrument](/wiki/String_instrument "String instrument") of the [violin family](/wiki/Violin_family "Violin family"). Its four strings are usually [tuned](/wiki/Intonation_(music) "Intonation (music)") in [perfect fifths](/wiki/Perfect_fifth "Perfect fifth"): from low to high, [C2, G2, D3 and A3](/wiki/Scientific_pitch_notation "Scientific pitch notation"). The [viola](/wiki/Viola "Viola")'s four strings are each an [octave](/wiki/Octave "Octave") higher. Music for the cello is generally written in the [bass clef](/wiki/Bass_clef "Bass clef"); the [tenor clef](/wiki/Tenor_clef "Tenor clef") and [treble clef](/wiki/Treble_clef "Treble clef") are used for higher-range passages.

Played by a *[cellist](/wiki/List_of_cellists "List of cellists")* or *violoncellist*, it enjoys a large solo repertoire [with](/wiki/Cello_sonata "Cello sonata") and [without accompaniment](/wiki/List_of_solo_cello_pieces "List of solo cello pieces"), as well as numerous [concerti](/wiki/Cello_concerto "Cello concerto"). As a solo instrument, the cello uses its whole range, from bass to soprano, and in [chamber music](/wiki/Chamber_music "Chamber music"), such as [string quartets](/wiki/String_quartet "String quartet") and the [orchestra](/wiki/Orchestra "Orchestra")'s [string section](/wiki/String_section "String section"), it often plays the bass part, where it may be reinforced an octave lower by the [double basses](/wiki/Double_bass "Double bass"). [Figured bass](/wiki/Figured_bass "Figured bass") music of the [Baroque era](/wiki/Baroque_music "Baroque music") typically assumes a cello, [viola da gamba](/wiki/Viol "Viol") or [bassoon](/wiki/Bassoon "Bassoon") as part of the [basso continuo](/wiki/Basso_continuo "Basso continuo") group alongside chordal instruments such as [organ](/wiki/Pipe_organ "Pipe organ"), [harpsichord](/wiki/Harpsichord "Harpsichord"), [lute](/wiki/Lute "Lute"), or [theorbo](/wiki/Theorbo "Theorbo"). Cellos are found in many other ensembles, from modern [Chinese orchestras](/wiki/Chinese_orchestra "Chinese orchestra") to [cello rock](/wiki/Cello_rock "Cello rock") bands.

The name *cello* is derived from the ending of the [Italian](/wiki/Italian_language "Italian language") *violoncello*,[[2]](#cite_note-2) which means "little [violone](/wiki/Violone "Violone")". [Violone](/wiki/Violone "Violone") ("big viola") was a large-sized member of [viol](/wiki/Viol "Viol") (viola da gamba) family or the [violin](/wiki/Violin "Violin") ([viola da braccio](/wiki/Viola_da_braccio "Viola da braccio")) family.
